<sense>
<definition> (abbrev. of קָאֵים) 
<italic>standing</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Y. Gen. XXIV, 13. Targ. Prov. XXIV, 16; a. e.—Ber. 2
<sup>a</sup> תנא היכא ק' דקתני וכ' where is the teacher of the Mishnah (I, </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition />
<notes> standing (what does he refer to), when he says, ‘From what time does the duty of reading the Sh’mʿa begin’? Ib. תנא אקרא ק' the teacher has in his mind the Biblical text (Deut. VI, 7). Taan. 2
<sup>a</sup> תנא התם ק' דקתני וכ' the teacher refers to what has been taught there (Ber. V, </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>2)</number>
<definition />
<notes> &c. Pes. 43
<sup>b</sup> מסתברא ק' באוכלין … ק' באוכלין מרבה נאכלין it stands to reason, where the text speaks of eaters (‘thou must’ or ‘must not eat’), you extend its scope to eaters, but when the text speaks of eaters, would you extend its scope to things to be (or not to be) eaten?; a. v. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S00025">
<head-word>קַב</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> קבב 
<italic>to hollow out, arch</italic>; cmp. גבב,
<language-reference>
<xref rid="A00083"> כבב)</xref></language-reference></definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>Kab</italic>, a measure of capacity, one sixth of a S’ah.</definition>
<notes> Sabb. 11
<sup>b</sup> הדיוט שהקק קב וכ' if an unskilled man caves out a Kab in a log (on the Sabbath); [Ar. refers to קַב 2, v. infra]. Tosef. B. Bath. V, 10 בכל מקום … קב וכ' everywhere (in all shops) they must make (keep) measures … of a Kab, half a Kab &c.; B. Bath. 89
<sup>b</sup>. Sot. 8
<sup>b</sup> a. e. קב וחצי קב וכ' minor measures of sin, v. סְאָה. Y. Hall. II, 58
<sup>c</sup> bot. קב טיברני dough of a Tiberian Kab of flour. B. Mets. 80
<sup>b</sup> קב לכתף one Kab (in addition to the load agreed upon) for a carrier is an unlawful overload; a. fr.—Sot. III, 4, a. e. בקב ותפלות, v. תִּפְלוּת. Snh. 29
<sup>b</sup> (in Chald. dict.) ההוא … קב רשו there was a man whom they nicknamed ‘a Kabful of notes of indebtedness’.—קב ונקי, v. נָקִי I.—
<italic>Du.</italic> קַבַּיִים; 
<plural-form>pl. קַבִּים, קַבִּין</plural-form>. B. Mets. 21
<sup>a</sup> ק' בשמונה וכ' if one finds two Kabs of fruits scattered within a radius of eight cubits.—Ḥall. II, 3 יעשנה ק' let him make his doughs Kab-wise (so as to be exempt from the priest’s share). Ib. 4. Kidd. 49
<sup>b</sup> עשרה ק' וכ' ten measures of &c. Ber. 22
<sup>a</sup> תשעה ק' nine Kabs of water poured over a person in place of immersion; a. fr.—Denom. קַבִּי, 
<plural-form>pl. קַבִּיִּים</plural-form>
<italic>pieces of dough containing a Kab of flour each</italic>. Ḥall. II, 3 אבל ק' אין להם חלק בשם (Y. ed. חלה) doughs made of a Kab each have no share in the name of 
<italic>ḥallah</italic></notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>a piece of wood hollowed out for the stump of a leg, a sort of artificial foot</italic> (cmp. אָנְקִטְמִין).</definition>
<notes> Yeb. 102
<sup>b</sup> (חלצה) בקב הקיטע if a woman performed the ceremony of Ḥălitsah (חֲלִיצָה) by taking off the 
<italic>Yabam’s</italic> artificial foot. Sabb. VI, 8; a. e.—
<italic>Pl.</italic> as ab. Ḥag. 4
<sup>a</sup> בעלי ק' stump-legged persons; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>cavity, the lower part of a trumpet</italic> or 
<italic>horn</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Kel. XI, 7 הקב שלה Mish. ed. a. Ar. (Talm. ed. הקו, ed. Dehr. הקב).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S00026">
<head-word>קַבָּא</head-word>

<sup>a</sup> אטו בק' דקירא וכ' am I stuck to you by (a gift of) a Kab of wax?, i.e. am I not free to form my own opinion? Yeb. 17
<sup>a</sup>, v. גַּנְדַּר I. Kidd. 79
<sup>b</sup>, v. כּוּל ch. Pes. 113
<sup>a</sup> ק' מארעא ולא כורא מאיגרא better a Kab from the ground, than a Kor from the roof, i.e. better a small profit at home, than a large one from abroad (for which you look out anxiously from your roof-top). Snh. 27
<sup>a</sup> bot. ק' דחושלא a Kab of peeled barley; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. קַבִּין; קַבַּיָּיא</plural-form>. Y. Ḥall. II, 58
<sup>d</sup> top ק' באתריהון רובעיא אזדרעון (read אתערעון, v. עֲרַע I) the Kabs (measures) in their place were enlarged by one fourth.—Esth. R. to I, 1 the world is shaped כאפי קַבָּאֵי (prob. to be read: קביא) like the outside of round measures.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S00057">
<head-word>קָבַל</head-word>
<hw-number>I</hw-number>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="H00083"> cmp. חבל </xref>a.
<xref rid="A00083"> חבר)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>

<italic>to seize; to join, meet, correspond</italic>.</definition>
<notes>]</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>קִבֵּל</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to receive, accept; to take an obligation upon one’s self; to contract, agree</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Zeb. II, 1 כל הזבחים שק' דמן זר וכ' all sacrifices whose blood was received (in a vessel) by a non-priest &c. Ib. 4 ק' והלך וזרק וכ' if he received the blood, or carried or sprinkled it with the thought of disposal at an unlawful time. Ib. 3; a. fr.—Ab. I, 1 משה ק' וכ' Moses received the (traditional) law from Sinai, and handed it over to &c. Ib. 4 קִבְּלוּ מהם (Var. ממנו) received the traditions from them. Ib. 3 לקַבֵּל וכ', v. עֶבֶד. Erub. 72
<sup>b</sup> מְקַבְּלֵי פרס; ib. 73
<sup>a</sup> מְקַבְּלוֹת, v. פְּרָס. Ab. I, 15 הוי מְקַבֵּל את כל וכ' receive every man &c., v. סֵבֶר. Keth. 58
<sup>a</sup> (a mnemonical formula) ק' מסר והלך if he (the betrothed) accepted (was satisfied to marry her in spite of blemishes discovered), or if the father handed his daughter over to the groom’s delegates, or if the father (or his delegates) went along with the groom’s delegates; Kidd. 11
<sup>a</sup>. Keth. 56
<sup>b</sup>, a. fr. ק' עליו אחריות if he assumed the guaranty. Dem. II, 2, sq. המקבל עליו וכ' he that obligates himself &c., v. נֶאֱמָן. Ex. R. s. 3 והם לא קבלו על וכ' and did they not receive (punishment) for what they did? Ib. אינו מקבל מוסר does not accept correction. Men. 96
<sup>b</sup>, a. fr. מקבל טומאה susceptible of levitical uncleanness; a. v. fr.—Esp. 
<italic>to take on lease, to rent a field</italic> either on shares (v. אָרִיס) or at a fixed rent (v. חָכִיר). B. Mets. IX, 1. Ib. 9 קִבְּלָהּ הימנו לשבע וכ' if he rented it of him for seven years. Ib. 10 קבלה הימנו שבע … בשבע וכ' if he rented it for ‘seven years at a rent of seven hundred Zuz’, the Sabbatical year is not included; a. fr.—ק' פנים, v. 
<italic>Hif.</italic>—ק' קיבולת, v. קִיבּוֹלֶת.—
<italic>Part. pass</italic>. מְקוּבָּל 
<italic>a</italic>) 
<italic>accepted, acceptable, well-liked, beloved</italic>. Ber. V, 5, v. טָרַף. Ib. 17
<sup>a</sup> ויהא מק' על הבריות and that he may be well-liked of men.—
<italic>b</italic>) 
<italic>holding a tradition</italic>. Peah II, 6 מק' אני מר' … שקבל וכ' I hold a tradition from R. M. who received it of &c.; Naz. 56
<sup>b</sup> כך מְקוּבְּלַנִי וכ'; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִקְבִּיל</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (with פנים or sub. פנים; interch.</definition>
<notes> with 
<italic>Pi.</italic>) 
<italic>to ask for a favorable reception, to visit, pay one’s respects to</italic>. Y. Erub. V, beg. 22
<sup>b</sup> אילולא דייו אלא שהיה מקבל פני רבו שכל המַקְבִּיל פני רבו כאילו מקבל וכ' (not דיין; = אילו לא עשה כלום אלא … דייו) had he done nothing (during the thirteen years of his waiting on his master) but greet his teacher, it were sufficient; for he that pays his respects to his teacher is considered as one waiting on the Divine Presence; Y. Snh. XI, 30
<sup>b</sup> top. Ḥag. 5
<sup>b</sup> אתם הִקְבַּלְתֶּם … תזכו להַקְבִּיל וכ' you have greeted a countenance that is seen but cannot see (a blind man), may you be permitted to greet the Countenance that sees and cannot be seen. Snh. 42
<sup>a</sup> אילמלא … להַקְבִּיל פני וכ' if Israelites were permitted to greet their Father in heaven only once a month &c.; כל המברך … כאילו מקבל וכ' saying the blessing over the new moon in its due time, is, as it were, greeting the Divine Presence; Yalk. Ex. 189 מקביל. Y. Ḥag. I, beg. 75
<sup>d</sup> והִקְבּילוּ ר' י' בבקיעין and waited upon (visited) R. J. in B’ḳiin; Y. Sot. III, 18
<sup>d</sup> bot.; Tosef. ib. VII, 9, 
<pgbrk id="pg1309" />והקבילו פני וכ'; Ḥag. 3
<sup>a</sup> הלכו להקביל פני וכ'; a. fr.—Sabb. 152
<sup>a</sup>, v. infra.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hof.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הוּקְבַּל</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (with פנים, or ל־) 
<italic>to be placed opposite, be admitted to the presence of</italic>, (a polite expression for:) 
<italic>to be visited</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sabb. 152
<sup>a</sup> מפני מה לא הוּקְבַּלְנוּ פניך … שהוּקְבְּלוּ אבותי לאבותיך early eds. (Ms. M. לא הוקבלו, incorr.; later eds. הִקְבַּלְנוּ … שהִקְבִּילוּ 
<italic>Hif.</italic>; v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) why were we not permitted to see you on the festive day, as my ancestors used to receive thy ancestors?</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִתְקַבֵּל, </binyan-form>
<binyan-name>Nithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִתְקַבֵּל</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be received, accepted</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sifra Vayikra, N’dab., ch. IV, Par. 4 הדם הדם שנ' בכלי ‘they shall sprinkle 
<italic>the</italic> blood’ (Lev. I, 5), the blood which has been received in a vessel. Zeb. 34
<sup>b</sup>, sq.; a. e.—Pesik. R. s. 44 ספק מִתְקַבֵּל ספק אינו מתקבל it is doubtful, will he or will he not be favorably received. Ab. d’R. N. ch. IV תפלתו מִתְקַבֶּלֶת ברצון his prayer was accepted with favor; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to make one’s self the recipient of, to receive, accept</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Keth. V, 1 הִתְקַבַּלְתִּי ממך וכ' I have received at thy hands (on account) one hundred &c. Gitt. VI, 1 הִתְקַבֵּל גט זה וכ' make thyself the receiver of this letter of divorce in behalf of my wife. <entry id="S00070">
<head-word>קַבָּלָה</head-word>
<hw-number>I</hw-number>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (קָבַל I) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>receiving, acceptance</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Pesik. R. s. 44 קַבָּלַת שבים the reception (in grace) of the repentant. Zeb. 13
<sup>a</sup> וק' מי פסלה does the receiving (of the sacrificial blood by a non-priest) make the sacrifice unfit? Ib. קבלת הדם receiving the blood in a vessel. Ib. I, 4 שלא בק' without the act of receiving the blood; a. fr.—Gitt. 62
<sup>b</sup> שליח לק' one deputed by the woman to receive the letter of divorce in her behalf, v. הוֹלָכָה. Ib. אק' referring to the reception of the letter of divorce in her behalf; a. fr.—Tosef. Kel. B. Mets. V, 10 בית ק' receptacle, v. קִיבּוּל.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>tradition, traditional law; post-Mosaic Scriptures</italic>, opp. to תורה or תורת משה.</definition>
<notes> R. Hash. 7
<sup>a</sup> דבר זה מתורת … מדברי ק' למדנו this (that the months are counted from Nisan) we learned not from the Law of Moses, but from the words of tradition (historical accounts, ref. to Zech. I, 7; Esth. II, 16 &c.). Ib. 19
<sup>a</sup> גדליה … דברי ק' הוא ודברי ק' וכ' the account of Gedaliah, son of A., is traditional (historical, Jer. XLI), and the words of tradition (post-Mosaic records) are as authoritative as the words of the Torah. Ḥag. 10
<sup>b</sup> דברי תורה מדברי ק' וכ' we must derive no interpretation of Mosaic laws from analogies of expression in post-Mosaic books (e.g. Am. V, 25 as illustrating the sense of Ex. V, 1); B. Kam. 2
<sup>b</sup>; Nidd. 23
<sup>a</sup>. Y. Ḥall. I, 57
<sup>b</sup> top ולמידין מן הק' can we derive a legal rule from a post-Mosaic book (Is. XXVIII, 25)?—Gen. R. s. 7 ומן הק' אתה מלקני wilt thou condemn me to lashes on an inference from a post-Mosaic book?; Tanḥ. Ḥuck. 6; a. fr.—[Ber. 62
<sup>a</sup>, v. קִבְלָא II.]—[In later Hebrew ק' 
<italic>Kabbalah, mystic lore</italic>.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sup>b</sup>, a. e. כל הקרב ביום אינו ק' אלא ביום וכ' whatever must be offered in day-time, becomes sacred (by being put in a sacred vessel) only in day-time &c. Meg. 23

<plural-form>Pl. קְדוֹשִׁים</plural-form>. Lev. R. l. c. Sabb. 86

<italic>Fem.</italic> קְדוֹשָׁה. Y. Maas. Sh. II, end, 53

<entry id="S00123">

<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (קָדַשׁ) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>holiness, sanctity, sacredness; chastity</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Yeb. II, 3, a. e. איסור ק', v. אִיסּוּר. Kidd. 55
<sup>a</sup>, a. fr. קְדוּשַּׁת הגוף an object which is consecrated as such (irredeemable), opp. ק' דמים that which is consecrated for its value (redeemable). Tem. 10
<sup>b</sup> משום דמפרש ק' על הולד because he has pronounced sanctity on the embryo (by dedicating the mother). Ib.
<sup>a</sup> אין ק' חלה על עיברין no sanctification takes effect on embryos (by the dedication of the mothers). Naz. VII, 1 נזיר שאין קְדוּשָּׁתוֹ קדושת עולם the Nazarite whose sanctification is not an everlasting one (it ceasing with the expiration of his vow). Ḥag. 3
<sup>b</sup> ק' ראשונה קִדְּשָׁהּ לשעתה as to the first consecration (of the holy land by Joshua), he consecrated it only for the time being (as long as inhabited and ruled by Israelites); Meg. 10
<sup>b</sup>, sq.; Zeb. 60
<sup>b</sup>; a. e.—Hor. 13
<sup>a</sup> זה גדל עמנו בק' וזה לא וכ' the one (the 
<italic>nathin</italic>, v. נָתִין) has grown up with us in holiness (under the influences of the Jewish religion), and the other (the proselyte) has not &c. Snh. 58
<sup>a</sup> לידתו בק' born in holiness (after his mother’s conversion); Yeb. 98
<sup>a</sup>, v. הוֹרָת; a. v. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>sanctification, proclaiming the holiness of the Lord, solemn public act connected with the idea of Israel’s priesthood</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Meg. 23
<sup>b</sup>; Ber. 21
<sup>b</sup> כל דבר שבק' לא יהא וכ' no sacred public act should be performed with less than ten persons.—Esp. קְדוּשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם 
<italic>a</italic>) 
<italic>sanctification of the Name, fidelity to the Jewish faith, martyrdom</italic>. Ib. 20
<sup>a</sup> מסרי נפשייהו אק' ה', v. מְסַר. Snh. 74
<sup>b</sup> מצווה על ק' ה' bound to sanctify the Name (with his life); a. fr.—
<italic>b</italic>) ק' השם, or קדושה 
<italic>the third section of the Prayer of Benedictions</italic> (תְּפִלָּה), 
<italic>praising the holiness of the Lord; the appeal to the congregation to join in the ‘holy, holy</italic> &c.’ (v. קָדוֹשׁ). R. Hash. IV, 5 סדר ברכות … וק' ה' the order of the benedictions (for the New Year’s Day) is: 
<italic>Aboth</italic> (v. אָב), 
<italic>G’buroth</italic> (v. גְּבוּרָה) and the sanctification. Ber. 21
<sup>b</sup> עד שלא יגיע … ק' before the reader reaches the 
<italic>ḳ’dushshah</italic>. Ib. אין היחיד אומר ק' one praying alone should not recite the 
<italic>ḳ’dushshah</italic>; a. fr.—קדושת היום (ק' שבת, ק' יום טוב), also ק' 
<italic>declaration of the sanctity of the day</italic> (
<italic>the Sabbath</italic> &c.) in prayer or at meals. R. Hash. l. c. ק' היום 
<italic>that section of the Prayer of Benedictions</italic> which closes with the benediction ‘who sanctifiest the day &c.’ Bets. 15
<sup>b</sup> לוו עלי וקדשו ק' היום וכ' borrow on my (the Lord’s) account and celebrate the sanctity of the day, and trust me &c. Ber. 33
<sup>b</sup> בין ק' שבת לק' יו"ט הבדלת thou hast made a distinction between the way of sanctifying the Sabbath and that of sanctifying the Holy Day. Pes. 105

<sense>

<sup>a</sup> כל שהרופא קוֹדְרוֹ (Ar. a. Ms. M. correct. קוֹדְדוֹ, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) such flesh as the physician cuts out; a. e.—Part. pass. (קָדוּד) קָדוּר. Ab. Zar. 32
<sup>a</sup> (expl. עור לבוב) כל שקרוע … וק' וכ' a hide which is slit open opposite the heart and cut out like an air-hole; Tosef. ib. IV (V), 7 כל שק' כנגד לבו Var. ed. Zuck. (text שנקוב, oth. ed. שקרוע). Ukts. II, 4 קְדוּרָה (ed. Dehr. קְדוּדָה) cut into, opp. שלמה.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>(קִדֵּד) קִדֵּר</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to cut through</italic>; (in measuring distances) 
<italic>to estimate the level distance between two places separated by mountains</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Erub. V, 4 (58
<sup>a</sup>) שמעתי שמְקַדְּרִין בהרים (Y. ed. Ven. שמְקַדְּדִין; v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 90) I have heard a tradition that in measuring Sabbath distances elevations are considered as cut through. Ib. 58
<sup>b</sup> כיצד מְקַדְּרִין וכ' how is the measuring done to obtain the tunnel distance? He who stands below holds the rope against his heart, while he who stands above holds the other end of the 
<pgbrk id="pg1318" />rope against his feet. Ib. אין מקדרין אלא בחבל וכ' only a rope of four cubits can be used for measuring &c. Ib. אין מקדרין לא בעגלה וכ' this method of measuring distances is not applied in the case of a slain body found in the field (v. עֶגְלָה), or for cities of refuge. Tosef. ib. VI (V), 11 מְקַדֵּר ועולה מק' ויורד וכ' we go up measuring the air-line and down again (on the other side), and consider the elevation as if it were cut through before us. Erub. 58
<sup>a</sup> מַקְדִּיר ועולה וכ'; Tosef. l. c. 12 מקדר. Y. ib. V, 22
<sup>d</sup> (repeatedly מְקַדְּדִין). Ib. מקדימין (corr. acc.). Y. Sot. V, 20
<sup>b</sup> bot. מקדדין; Y. Macc. II, end, 32
<sup>a</sup> מקדרין; a. fr.—Y. Keth. XIII, 36
<sup>b</sup> top מקדר ויוצא וכ' he may cut his way through the vines and get out (v. פָּסַג).—[Pes. 11
<sup>b</sup> מקדרין, read: מקרדין, v. קָרַד.]</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> (denom. of קָדֵר or קַדָּר) 
<italic>to make pots, pretend to be a potter</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ruth R. to I, 1 (s. 2), v. קַדָּרוּת.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>

<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to cut through; to penetrate</italic>.</definition>

<sup>a</sup>, v. supra. Nidd. 56
<sup>b</sup>; Tosef. ib. VI, 13 מַקְדִּיר, v. גָּלַד; [perh. fr. קָדַר II, 
<italic>becomes dull</italic>].</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
